prompt_text: Paint an orthographic transparent-background asset atlas using the first two references as the ONLY source for object identity, palette, texture, block layout, and up/down state; use the third reference only for camera geometry. Exactly 5 columns by 2 rows, one complete isolated stair per cell, no labels, no shadows, generous gaps. Row 1 is the UP stone stair, row 2 the DOWN stair. Columns left to right: FRONT end elevation, RIGHT long-side elevation, LEFT opposite long-side elevation, BOTTOM overhead-camera underside, REAR opposite end elevation. Keep the source square footprint, black outlines, tan cut-stone blocks, red side stones, blue inset stair treads. Preserve source heading: UP rises toward rear; DOWN descends toward rear. Make all four elevations share one plausible stair height and groundline: FRONT and REAR are flat rectangular end faces looking straight along the stair axis, showing stacked horizontal stone courses and the correct high/low terminal step, not broad tread surfaces; RIGHT and LEFT are true level side profiles with a clear stepped/rising silhouette across depth, showing the same full rise as front/rear and no broad top plan. BOTTOM is a full square solid stone underside with opaque tan/gray substrate and support footprint, no blue tread faces, no grass. Do not change the TOP; it is not in this atlas. All surfaces must read as this same physical staircase in the two opposite rise directions. Crisp chunky pixel art matching source, no extra objects or scenery.
